name: Find and Replace
summary: Literal find and replace with case, whole word and multiline options.
about: Finds a piece of text and replaces every occurrence, treating the text to find as literal characters rather than a regular expression, and the replacement text as literal characters rather than a pattern with dollar-sign sequences. Case sensitivity, whole-word matching and matching across a line break are all optional.
supports: Whole-word matching, where a Unicode letter, mark, number or connector punctuation counts as part of a word
Multiline matching, where the text to find spans a line break
A literal dollar-sign sequence in the replacement, inserted exactly as typed
Regular-expression symbols in the text to find, treated as ordinary characters
A count of the number of non-overlapping replacements made
An empty text to find, which leaves the input unchanged
limits: This is literal find and replace, not a regular-expression engine: no wildcards, character classes or capture groups are read from the text to find.
With multiline off, a text to find that contains a line break is refused rather than silently never matching.
With multiline on, CRLF line endings in both the input and the text to find are normalised to a single line feed before matching, and the output uses a line feed too.
Whole-word boundaries follow this tool's own definition of a word character (a Unicode letter, mark, number or connector punctuation); punctuation such as a hyphen is never treated as part of a word.
ambiguities: "Whole word" has no single universal definition. This tool treats a Unicode letter, mark, number or connector punctuation as a word character and everything else as a boundary, which matches how most text editors define it.
apiNotes: The replacement is inserted through a replacer function, never a string replacement pattern, so a dollar sign in the replacement text is never expanded. A bad option, such as a multiline text to find with multiline off, throws `FindReplaceError`.
testNotes: No standard defines literal find and replace, so standards is empty; tests assert behaviour against hand-worked examples covering literal matching of regular-expression symbols, a dollar-sign replacement text, case sensitivity, whole-word boundaries including accented letters and digits, multiline matching, and non-overlapping match counting.
